chapter: Ellington's later years and Quincy Jones
title: Ellington at the piano and humming when the band cooked
summary: Ellington hummed and hit chords behind soloists when he was pleased, and Jackson says he was a great accompanist who knew where you were.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: They would fire up like nothing you ever heard in your life. And Duke would sit there and whenever you could see him with that frown on his face and he would start to humming that one tone, the band was knocking him out then and he was very pleased.
I've seen him with his head like this.
And he'd get to hitting that piano and hitting them chords all in the middle, all in between.
One of the greatest -- to me one of the greatest accompanists, for a jazz soloist, and he would hit a chord to let you know exactly where you was or where he wanted you to be --
-- and you would play that change. He knew where you was at all times.
